title: The Mood of the Moor
welcome_lead: Weather, walls and time of day all carry the writer's hidden message.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on setting details building mood.
final_note: You can now read mood from setting clues.

walkthroughs.body_html: When 'the heavens wept' as a character grieves, the writer uses pathetic fallacy — weather echoes emotion.
Smell of damp leaves, crunch of gravel, taste of salt — sensory details make settings vivid and tug at mood.
A locked attic can symbolise secrets; an open field, freedom. Setting can carry symbolic weight.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a theme and a symbol?
